spec.concept: With n random IDs from N choices, the chance of a repeat grows with n squared, so collisions come far sooner than n/N suggests.
spec.definition: A hash collision is when two different inputs get the same hash value or ID.

prediction.prompt: You give 1,000 files random IDs drawn from 1,000,000 possible IDs. What is the chance at least two files share an ID?

extremes.watch: With only 100,000 possible IDs, a repeat among 1,000 files is almost certain (99.3%).
With 10 million possible IDs the chance drops to about 4.9%.

misconceptions.label: 1,000 out of a million is tiny
misconceptions.why_tempting: 1,000 IDs fill only 0.1% of the space, so a clash feels near impossible.
misconceptions.refutation: Every pair can clash: 1,000 IDs make about 500,000 pairs, so the chance is about 39%.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified

misconceptions.label: Collisions are basically certain
misconceptions.why_tempting: After hearing about the birthday paradox, it's tempting to overshoot.
misconceptions.refutation: With 1,000 IDs it's about 39%; it passes 50% around 1,180 IDs.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified
